nodes.label: AWS Security Hub Source Mode
nodes.source_location: A GitHub Action that syncs AWS Security Hub or Snowflake findings with Jira

nodes.label: Stable Global Finding Identity
nodes.rationale: TOOL_NAME, FISMA_ID, RESOURCE_ID, and FINDING_ID form the durable identity used to prevent duplicate Jira issues across repeated runs.

nodes.label: Snowflake Findings Provenance Label
nodes.rationale: The fixed snowflake-findings label distinguishes Jira issues created from Snowflake from manual issues and tickets created by other systems.

nodes.label: Canonical FISMA Ownership Boundary
nodes.rationale: Exactly one FISMA ID or acronym defines the authoritative population and Jira ownership boundary for each Snowflake reconciliation run.

nodes.label: All Open Findings for One FISMA
nodes.rationale: Snowflake mode queries every OPEN finding for one FISMA boundary across all tools and severities to keep the authoritative comparison stable.
nodes.norm_label: all open findings for one fisma

nodes.label: Snowflake Maximum Row Safety Ceiling
nodes.rationale: Fetching one row beyond the configured maximum allows the action to abort before Jira reconciliation rather than act on a truncated population.

nodes.label: Snowflake Auto-Close Completeness Gate
nodes.rationale: Auto-close remains disabled until every expected tool supplies a complete authoritative result and absence from the view reliably means resolution.

nodes.label: Source-Sensitive Auto-Close Default
nodes.author: MAC-FC
nodes.rationale: Auto-close defaults true for the legacy AWS mode and false for Snowflake so the new global-view lifecycle is piloted conservatively.

nodes.label: Snowflake Global Findings to Jira Integration Discovery
nodes.norm_label: snowflake global findings to jira integration discovery

nodes.label: Integration Evidence Classification
nodes.rationale: Repository proof, user-provided context, platform documentation, and live pilot evidence are separated to avoid presenting a local proof of concept as deployed integration evidence.

nodes.label: Managed Jira Issue Boundary
nodes.source_location: Section 7.2 Snowflake provenance and FISMA ownership
nodes.rationale: Jira reconciliation is restricted by project, global-security-findings, snowflake-findings, the exact FISMA ownership label, and non-ignored status so unrelated tickets cannot be changed.

nodes.label: No Configuration-Derived Reconciliation Scope
nodes.source_location: Section 7.2 Snowflake provenance and FISMA ownership
nodes.rationale: No snowflake-scope label has been deployed; provenance plus one exact FISMA ownership label replaces mutable tool, severity, delay, and view-derived scope hashing without requiring migration.

nodes.label: Complete Authoritative Source Result
nodes.rationale: A successful open-findings query alone cannot authorize closure; every expected tool must prove that the result is complete and authoritative.

nodes.label: Write-Enabled Pilot P0 Gaps
nodes.source_location: Section 10 Prototype gaps and decisions required

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Snowflake and Jira Identities
nodes.rationale: Dedicated service identities minimize access to only the Snowflake view and required Jira project operations.

nodes.label: Scheduled Snowflake View to Jira GitHub Workflow
nodes.norm_label: scheduled snowflake view to jira github workflow

nodes.label: FISMA-Centric Reconciliation Model
nodes.rationale: When exactly one authoritative job owns all tools for a FISMA system, stable FISMA ownership is simpler than a configuration-derived scope and avoids orphaning tickets when filters change.

nodes.label: Snowflake Provenance and FISMA Reconciliation Model
nodes.rationale: A fixed snowflake-findings label plus FISMA ownership and stable finding identity distinguishes Snowflake tickets without changing the identity contract.
nodes.norm_label: snowflake provenance and fisma reconciliation model

nodes.label: SonarQube Snapshot Completeness Risk
nodes.rationale: Ordinary delay leaves prior persistent rows stale; false disappearance requires an incomplete snapshot to be treated as complete or an upstream lifecycle error.
